title: Real-time bike demand *forecasting.*
summary: A complete MLOps system for bike-rental demand: validated data ingestion, scheduled batch prediction, automatic retraining with safe model promotion, and drift monitoring.
dek: A small model inside a full production loop: every file is validated, every prediction is traced to a model version, and a new model only replaces the old one if it is at least as good.
cardMetric: Validated, retrained, and monitored end to end
body:
Training a model is the easy part. This project is about everything around it: making sure bad data never reaches the model, serving predictions reliably, retraining when enough new data arrives, and noticing when the world drifts away from the training data.

:: 8 | data-quality expectations on every file
:: 7 | types of data errors injected to test them
:: 3 | scheduled Airflow pipelines
:: 1 | command to start the whole stack

## The system

=> Ingest: new 10-row files arrive every minute and are validated with Great Expectations for completeness, validity, consistency, schema, and type
=> Triage: clean rows go to the database; bad rows are quarantined, scored by severity, and serious problems trigger a Teams alert
=> Predict: every two minutes, new clean files are sent in one batch to the FastAPI model service, and each prediction is stored with its model version
=> Retrain: every hour, if enough new data has arrived, a candidate Random Forest is trained and logged to MLflow
=> Promote safely: the candidate replaces the champion only if its R² is within 0.01 of the champion and inference stays under two seconds
=> Monitor: Grafana dashboards track data quality, feature drift against the training baseline, and predictions per model version

## Testing the guard rails

To prove the validation works, a corruption script deliberately injects seven kinds of errors, such as missing columns, out-of-range values, invalid categories, wrong data types, duplicates, and inconsistent fields, and the pipeline has to catch them.

> Alerts are tiered on purpose: low-severity issues are logged but not sent, to avoid alert fatigue.

## Engineering practices

- [ ] **Model registry:** the serving model is always the MLflow model tagged as champion, with a local fallback
- [ ] **Traceability:** every stored prediction records which model version produced it
- [ ] **CI/CD:** linting and tests on every pull request, and automatic versioned releases
- [ ] **Reproducible:** the full stack, from database to dashboards, starts with Docker Compose

The data is an hourly bike-sharing dataset of 17,379 records, streamed into the system in small files to simulate a live feed.
